props.title: Her
props.initialSlug: Man falls in love with his AI operating system

sections.content: **Her (2013)** (2013) masterfully explores modern loneliness through Theodore's (Joaquin Phoenix) relationship with an AI operating system. Spike Jonze crafts a near-future Los Angeles that feels warmly familiar rather than coldly dystopian, using soft pastels and high-waisted fashion to create an inviting world where human-AI romance seems natural. The film shares DNA with **Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind** (2004) in its intimate examination of unconventional love, while its gentle sci-fi elements echo **Ex Machina** (2014)'s questions about consciousness and connection.

sections.content: The theme of technology mediating human connection runs through contemporary cinema, but rarely with Her's empathy and nuance. While **Black Mirror** episodes (2011-2019) often present cautionary tales about tech dependency, and **The Social Network** (2010) examines how digital innovation can ironically lead to isolation, Her suggests technology might actually help us understand ourselves better. Samantha's evolution mirrors Theodore's emotional growth, creating a uniquely symbiotic relationship that transcends typical AI narratives. SUBHEAD: Love in the Digital Age

Her's influence appears in later films like **Creative Control** (2015) and **Marjorie Prime** (2017), which similarly explore virtual relationships and artificial companionship. The film's visual style - particularly its use of intimate close-ups and soft focus photography - creates a tactile warmth unusual in sci-fi, more reminiscent of **Before Sunset** (2004) than typical genre fare. This approach has influenced how subsequent films depict human-technology interaction, seen in works like **Ex Machina** (2014) and **Archive** (2020).
